column2: Word has come from across the sea: [From.GetTitledFirstName] is gathering a great host to take Ulthuan. Corsairs, Witch Elves and the scum of the Black Arks are flocking to [From.GetHerHis] banner, and the Dark Elves have not forgotten the way to our shores.

Word has come from across the sea: [From.GetTitledFirstName] is gathering a great host to take back Ulthuan. Spearmen, mages and the knights of the Inner Kingdoms are flocking to [From.GetHerHis] banner, and the Asur mean to see the Phoenix Throne freed of us.
We must prepare.

You waited too long. Month by month the host you gathered has lost its hunger for Ulthuan and turned to its own squabbles. The corsairs have gone back to raiding, the Witch Elves to their temples, and there is no army left to cross the sea.

You waited too long. Month by month the host you gathered has lost its resolve, the princes arguing over whether this was ever the right moment to strike. One by one they have gone home, and there is no army left to cross the sea.
Faithless, spineless fools!
Another time, then.
A great host of raiders has answered your call. They sharpen their blades on the docks and wait for the order to sail for Ulthuan.
A great host of warriors has answered your call. They drill on the shore and wait for the order to sail for Ulthuan.
Good.
A famous corsair lord has come to your court with his own crews and a pack of ships behind him. He offers his blades for the war on Ulthuan, in return for a fair share of the slaves and the plunder.
A famous captain has come to your court with his household warriors and ships of his own. He offers his sword to free Ulthuan from the Druchii, asking nothing but a place in the vanguard.
Welcome, captain.
A small band of raiders has answered your call. They wait on the docks for the order to sail for Ulthuan.
A small company of warriors has answered your call. They wait on the shore for the order to sail for Ulthuan.

Your prisoner [From.GetFirstName] is thrown into the pit, and the cold one is let loose soon after. It circles, hissing, tasting the air, and then it lunges. The screaming does not last long. Your court watches every moment of it.
Who else is hungry?
Your jailer has had you thrown into a pit. Something cold and scaled moves in the dark below you, and it is hungry.
No! NO!
Your prisoner [From.GetFirstName] is chained in the middle of the square for all to see. At your call the dragon comes down out of the sky, and the fire takes [From.GetHerHim] before the jaws do.
Your jailer has had you chained in the square like a goat. The crowd falls silent, and a great shadow passes over the sun.

Your prisoner [From.GetFirstName] is chained in the middle of the square for all to see. At your call the griffon drops onto [From.GetHerHim], pins [From.GetHerHim] with its talons and begins to feed while [From.GetSheHe] is still screaming.
Your jailer has had you chained in the square. You hear the beat of great wings, and then the shriek of the griffon.
Your prisoner [From.GetFirstName] is dragged into the yard where your wyvern is chained. The beast takes [From.GetHerHim] in one bite, then a second, and the court remembers who it serves.
Your jailer has decided to feed you to a wyvern. You can smell its breath from across the yard.
The Witch King Is Dead

So it has come to pass: not a man but a woman versed in the arcane arts has slain the Witch King. For millennia Malekith forbade men of his realm to touch magic, for fear of the old prophecy that a sorcerer would end him, and it seems he read it wrong all along. His throne in Naggarond is empty, and the Druchii will soon tear each other apart for it.

So it has come to pass: a sorcerer has slain the Witch King, just as the old prophecy foretold. For millennia Malekith had every gifted man of Naggaroth killed or hollowed, and in the end it did him no good. His throne in Naggarond is empty, and the Druchii will soon tear each other apart for it.

So it has come to pass: no sorcerer, but a common blade has slain the Witch King. For millennia Malekith had every gifted man of Naggaroth killed or hollowed, so afraid was he of the old prophecy that a sorcerer would end him. He never thought to fear plain steel. His throne in Naggarond is empty, and the Druchii will soon tear each other apart for it.
The son of Aenarion is no more.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has grown weary of [From.GetHerHis] squabbling subjects. [From.GetHerHis] spies and informers are everywhere now, and lords who spoke too boldly are vanishing in the night. You and your fellow conspirators have thought it wise to forget your faction, for now.
Our time will come.

Another of your subjects has been found out: [From.GetTitledFirstName] has the gift, and has been practising the dark arts in secret. Why would a man hide such a thing, if not to grow strong enough to kill you?
There is no doubt any more. Your own son [From.GetFirstName] has the gift of a sorcerer, and he hid it from you. Why would he, if not to plot against your throne?
I will not die by your sorcery.
The prophecy will not be fulfilled. Not even by you, my son.
Send him to the Convent. Let them cut it out of him.
The sorcerer is hollowed: his gift is torn out and he will never cast a spell again.

The Witch King has learned of your dealings with the dark arts. His assassins come for you in the night, and before you can speak a single word of power their blades are in your back, again and again.
Hhhgghh...

The Witch King has learned of your dealings with the dark arts. His guards drag you to Ghrond, where the hags of the Convent bind you on a cold stone slab and tear the gift out of you. You live, but the winds are gone, and you will never forget whose mercy that was.
It is... gone.
The End of the Witch King's Empire

With the Witch King gone, not one of the Druchii despots will recognise you, or anyone else, as their overlord. Malekith held his realm together for millennia by setting the Dark Elves against each other, and now the price of his rule falls on you.

You have been cast down, and none of the Druchii will recognise anyone else in your place. For millennia you held your realm together by setting the Dark Elves against each other, and now they are turning on each other with no one to stop them.

With the Witch King gone, not one of the Druchii despots will recognise anyone else as overlord. Malekith held Naggaroth together for millennia by setting the Dark Elves against each other, and now the Land of Chill will drown in their feuds.
Curses!
Ungrateful wretches.
My time is now!
The false king falls at last!
Interesting.
The Return of Naggaroth

Since the Witch King fell, our people have torn each other apart to take his place. Now I hold his old capital and enough of the Land of Chill to put real weight behind my claim. Soon all of Naggaroth will kneel.

Your birthright was slipping away. Your treacherous vassals plotted to oust you, but none of them could rule the Druchii, and in the chaos they turned on each other. Now you sit on your throne again, though your authority may never fully recover from the humiliation.
Since the Witch King fell, our people have torn each other apart to take his place. Now one of them has seized his old capital and enough of the Land of Chill to put real weight behind the claim.
Since the Witch King fell, the Druchii have torn each other apart to take his place. Now one of them has seized his old capital and enough of the Land of Chill to put real weight behind the claim.
Today Naggaroth, tomorrow Ulthuan.
I must stay vigilant.
Killing only each other was getting dull anyway.
Troubling.
Interesting.
Every able young man of Naggaroth owes the Witch King fifty years in his host. Your time has come. Your lord must give you up to the officers from Naggarond.
I will tell my lord.

Every able young man of Naggaroth owes the Witch King fifty years in his host. [From.GetFirstName] has come of age, and the officers from Naggarond will soon arrive to take [From.GetHerHim]. Gold in the right hands could make them forget [From.GetHerHim], but the Witch King would hear of it.
Let him serve.
The officers can be persuaded.
[From.GetFirstName] has not stood in the way of the Witch King's levy. It is time to leave for Naggarond. You will not see home again for fifty years, if you see it at all.
For the Witch King.
[From.GetFirstName] has used bribes and threats on the officers from Naggarond to keep you at court. It seems you will escape the levy entirely.
How fortunate.

Your fifty years in the Witch King's host are over. You have learned to trust the warriors of your company with your life, and they you. The captains of the Black Guard have watched you and offer you a place among them, sworn to Malekith until death. Or you could go home and take up your place as a lord of Naggaroth.
I will swear the oath.
Fifty years is enough.
Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] will not come home. [From.GetSheHeCap] has sworn [From.GetHerHim]self to the Black Guard of Naggarond for life.
So be it.
Life in the Witch King's host is no less cutthroat than the rest of Druchii society. You did not have what it takes, and your company will not grieve.
No...
Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has heard the call of Khaine and means to become a Witch Elf. Khaine is a jealous god: once she is his bride, she may never belong to anyone else.
Khaine shall have her.
I forbid it.

You have given yourself to the Lord of Murder, cast off everything you owned and proclaimed yourself his bride. For years to come you will learn the rites and secrets of the Witch Elves, so that you may serve your god better. Not every bride lives to finish.
Blood for Khaine!
No mercy and no love. The Lord of Murder delights in death and suffering, and in the rivers of blood spilled in his honour you feel nothing but hunger for more.
The horrors of the temple have tempered your soul like steel in a forge. You have seen everything a mortal can fear, and none of it frightens you any more.
The endless rites and the blood-soaked raids have made you stronger and faster than any ordinary elf. Few could hold their own against you now.
Khaine rules over death, and none escape him. The greatest warrior and the wisest sorcerer alike pay him tribute in the end. You understand that now, with all your heart.
Blades and daggers, day and night. They leave their mark.
Every Witch Elf is a bride of Khaine, and he lets no man touch them. But you have found another kind of comfort in his halls, warmer and softer than anything his statue can offer.
Through discipline and practice your mind has opened to the designs of the Lord of Murder: new ways to kill, new ways to win, dreams of slaughter on a grand scale.
In the frenzy of last night's rite, some of your fellow pupils were overcome by Khaine's bloodlust and fell on you. You could not fight them all off, and you barely survived.
Blood and death sing in your veins. You hear Khaine whispering to you now, naming his next victims, and you cannot stop listening.
Their screams are music.
It is others who should be afraid.
Their blood for my strength!
Blood for Khaine!
Every scar is an offering.
Hmm.
Show me the way.
Grrnnhh!
I will do your bidding, Lord of Murder.

The years have passed, and for all your fervour the Lord of Murder has found you wanting. An assassin of the temple comes for you in the dark, and as the light leaves your eyes a cold whisper tells you that you have failed your god.
Hghh...

For years you have trained, bathed in the blood of your enemies and laid their beating hearts on the altar of Khaine. The Lord of Murder looks on you with favour, and your sisters of the coven treat you as one of their own.

You do not remember your parents, only the temple: the knives, the poisons, the long nights in the dark. Now the priestesses have blooded you in the Cauldron and sent you out into the world, a Khainite assassin with no master but the Lord of Murder.
As it should be.

It is Death Night. The Witch Elves come silent and deadly through the halls, but it is not blood they want tonight. You are snatched from your cradle, carried shrieking to the altar of Khaine and baptised in blood. You will grow up among the brides of the Lord of Murder, and if you live, you will be one of his assassins.

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] is gone! The Witch Elves came on Death Night and took [From.GetHerHim] from [From.GetHerHis] cradle. Many children do not survive the temple of Khaine, but [From.GetFirstName] may yet be strong and blessed enough to grow into a deadly assassin.
For the glory of Khaine.

On patrol along the Blackspine, [druchii_hero.GetTitledFirstName] fell on a warband of northern marauders and cut [druchii_hero.GetHerHis] way through their ranks. A dozen heads came back to court on spears, and the rest were left for the crows. Khaine has surely smiled on [druchii_hero.GetHerHim].
The court shall honour [druchii_hero.GetHerHim].
I could have done as well. Better, even.

[druchii_coward.GetTitledFirstName]'s patrol was caught in an ambush in the passes, and [druchii_coward.GetSheHe] ran, leaving [druchii_coward.GetHerHis] warriors to die screaming behind [druchii_coward.GetHerHim]. The whole court knows it. Khaine despises a coward, and so does every Druchii who has ever drawn a knife.
That was ill done. Let the shame be [druchii_coward.GetHerHis] punishment.
To the cells. I will deal with [druchii_coward.GetHerHim] myself, slowly.
Get out of my sight, and out of my lands.
Give [druchii_coward.GetHerHim] to the brides of Khaine. Let [druchii_coward.GetHerHis] heart feed the Bloody-Handed God.

Your liege's court is crowded with idle mouths, and every one of them stands between you and favour. [druchii_herd_victim.GetTitledFirstName] is the weakest of them: no friends worth fearing, no wits worth respecting. A few drops of black lotus in [druchii_herd_victim.GetHerHis] wine, and there is one fewer to compete with.
The herd must be thinned.
Not yet. Patience is a knife too.

[druchii_herd_victim.GetTitledFirstName] was found dead in [druchii_herd_victim.GetHerHis] chambers, lips black with poison. Your spymaster is quite certain whose hand poured it: [From.GetTitledFirstName], who has been seen smiling at the funeral rites. In the courts of Naggaroth such things are hardly rare, but it was done under your roof.
Only the strong survive. Let it pass.
Such cunning deserves a reward. Quietly.
Poison in my halls is my right, not theirs. Seize [From.GetHerHim].

Your schemes have crossed those of [druchii_rival.GetTitledFirstName], and neither of you is the forgiving kind. From now on you must watch every cup and every shadow, and work towards [druchii_rival.GetHerHis] ruin before [druchii_rival.GetSheHe] works towards yours.
I will prevail. I always do.
Whispers at court say that [From.GetTitledFirstName] and [druchii_rival.GetTitledFirstName] have become bitter rivals. It should be amusing to see which of them is still breathing in a few years.
Let them fight it out. The strongest will survive.
Do not trouble me with such squabbles again.

A slaver from Karond Kar comes to court with a chained line of Dawi taken from the mountains of the Old World. A hundred of them, he swears, stubborn and strong, and a Dwarf at the whip will build for twenty years before the work kills him. He asks five hundred gold.
A bargain. Put them to work in my capital.
Not now.
Do not bring me slavers again.

A corsair captain comes to your hall with a prize: a Bretonnian knight, taken half dead after a raid on his coast. He asks only fifty gold for the man. A knight of Bretonnia is surely worth far more than that in ransom, or as a gift on the altar of Khaine.
A fine bargain. Throw [From.GetHerHim] in the cells.
I have no use for [From.GetHerHim].

You remember the sorceress, the lightning and the fall from your horse. After that there are only fever dreams, salt and the creak of a ship in the dark. Now you wake in a black cell, so cold that your breath freezes on the iron. Somewhere above, someone is laughing.
W-wait... is this... Naggaroth?
I will get out. And when I do...

You are a noble of Naggaroth, and the cold seas are wide. With a ship, a hungry crew and a little gold you can sail for the coasts of the weaker races and come home with slaves and plunder, for the glory of Khaine and the Witch King.
Find me a ship. I shall return with slaves and gold!
Not now.
You have been maimed, and a cripple cannot lead a boarding party. It is time to sail home and let others bleed on the decks, while you guard your wealth and power from your hall.
Curses! But hate will carry me on.
Your wounds are too deep to fight on. The crew turn the prow for home, where you can heal and count your plunder.
Set sail for home.
Your hold is heavy with plunder and your treasure chests are full. A wise raider knows when to stop before the sea takes it all back. Then again, a wise raider would never have sailed at all.
Home, and put this wealth to good use.
No. There is always more.
Do you wish to stop raiding and sail for home?
Yes, turn for home.
No, the hunt goes on.
One night off the coast of Bretonnia you see lights ahead: a fishing village, asleep and unguarded, as far as you can tell from the sea.
Tell the crew. We bathe in blood tonight!
No. I seek greater prey.
You slip ashore in silence and circle the village before the first scream goes up. The slaughter is glorious. By dawn the houses are burning and the hold is full of weeping captives in chains.
Blood and souls for Khaine!

You are hardly ashore when a bell starts ringing, and torches come pouring out of a camp beyond the village: a lance of Bretonnian knights, mounted and ready. The village was bait, or simply unlucky for you.
Back to the ships, quickly!
Three sails on the horizon, a merchant convoy of the human kingdoms. They are no warships, but there are three of them.
Full sail! Ready the boarding ropes!
Three is too many.
Spotting your black sail, the merchants turn to meet you. Brave fools, they actually mean to fight.
Bolt throwers, cut down their masts!
Three against one. We withdraw.

Your bolt throwers shred the sails of two ships, leaving them dead in the water. Your corsairs board the third, and then the others, one by one. The crews go into the hold in chains, and the cargo is rich.
And such a cargo!
Your bolts fly wide, and one of the merchants carries a catapult. Stones crash into the sea around you, and one smashes through the rail a yard from where you stand.
Turn about! We will outsail these scows!
An Eagle Ship of Ulthuan has seen your sail and comes on fast, white wings on a grey sea. You cannot outrun a warship of your hated cousins. You will have to fight.
Prepare to repel boarders. Bolt throwers, fire at will!

Your bolts smash the Asur repeater on its mount, and when they try to board, the hatred of your corsairs is more than their discipline can bear. Soon the white decks run red and the last of the cousins go over the side.
Take their ship. It will fetch a fine price in Clar Karond.

A long duel of bolt throwers leaves both ships battered. Their sails are torn, but yours are worse, and they are closing. One last shot at their main mast is all that stands between you and an Asur blade.
I will take that shot myself.

The sea heaves, and a long black neck rises out of the swell beside your ship: a sea dragon, scarred and huge. The hides of such beasts make the cloaks every corsair wears, and the scales of this one would buy a ship.
Harpoons! Bring it alongside!
Let it pass. The sea is wide.

It takes a dozen harpoons and two of your crew, but at last the sea dragon thrashes its last and floats belly up in a slick of black blood. The corsairs set to work on the hide before the sharks come.
A worthy prize.
The sea dragon snaps a harpoon line, coils around your prow and drags half the ship under. Men are thrown screaming into the water, and the deck tilts beneath you.
Cut the lines! Cut them!
They may have taken Nagarythe from you for now, but it is yours by birth and by right. You will never give up your claim to the land of your fathers.
It will be mine again.

For two hundred and fifty gold the Convent of Sorceresses will let one of its daughters serve your house for ten years: in your armies, on your council, and in matters of magic. Her first loyalty stays with the Witch King, of course. It always will.
Send the offer.
No.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] offers you two hundred and fifty gold to serve [From.GetHerHis] house as Sorceress for ten years. Do you accept?
Gold is gold. I accept.
No.
I accept your offer, my [Root.GetLordLady]. Rest assured, I will serve you in all ways while our contract lasts, and devote myself to your house, saving only my first loyalty to Malekith and Morathi.
Excellent.
Ten years have passed, and [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s contract with your house has run out. She will stay for another two hundred and fifty gold, or go back to the Convent.
Pay her. She has earned it.
Let her go.
In Naggaroth a dragon egg is nothing but power waiting to be taken. Eaten raw, they say, it gives the one who eats it a little of the dragon's strength.
This power shall be mine.
On second thought, that would be a waste of a dragon.
The black dragons of Naggaroth are fearsome beasts, and with gold, a name and ten years to spare you can raise one of your own. The beast-breeders of Clar Karond have an egg for sale.
A dragon rider I shall be.
On second thought, a Cold One will do.
A year has passed, and your dragon egg has cracked open. The newborn rears up, spreads its wings and tries a mighty roar, but only mewls like a kitten. It has a long way to go.
A long way to go yet...
The egg is gone, and that is that.
Nine years have passed, and your dragon is grown. It has bonded with you and been trained for war, and now it is a mount to make the bravest army break and run.
Let them fail their nerve and flee.
The hatchling is gone, and that is that.
A black dragon egg has come into your hands. You could raise it, or sell it for a quick profit.
Something this powerful I keep.
Sell it.
A black dragon hatchling has come into your hands. You could keep training it, or sell it for a quick profit.
Something this powerful I keep.
Sell it.

To honour Khaine properly you must invite every one of your vassals to your hall. Your scribe writes the letters in red ink and the riders leave at dawn. The guests will expect a table worthy of a lord of Naggaroth, a gift for your consort and blood for the Lord of Murder.
It will be a feast they never forget.
Your vassals are invited to the Feast of Khaine. It begins in twelve days.

Vassal,

You will attend my Feast of Khaine. Come with your retinue and your blades, and bring a gift worthy of my table.

Your Liege,
[From.GetFullName]
Of course I shall attend.
I have more pressing matters at home.
Dread liege, I regret that I cannot come to your feast. Matters of greater importance keep me at home.\n\n[From.GetFullName]
Insolent cur. It was not a request.

Tradition demands that a Druchii brings a slave to the Feast of Khaine as a gift for [Root.GetHerHis] consort. The slave markets of Har Ganeth are full this season, but a fine specimen does not come cheap.
A beautiful Asur slave.
A sturdy Dawi specimen.
A human wretch will do.
No more slaves this year.
I will spend the gold on my lover instead.
Your lover will expect a gift at the Feast of Khaine as well. A slave given in front of the whole court says more than any whispered promise. It also says a great deal to your consort.

At the height of the feast comes the ceremony of gifts. One by one the slaves are dragged forward in their chains and presented, while the whole court watches who receives what, and who receives nothing.
Let the gifts speak for me.
Your steward wants to know what you will serve your guests. Your vassals will judge you by your table, and they will talk about it for years.
Slow-roasted hearts and the finest Tilean wine.
Cold One steaks and good Naggarothi wine.
Fish, black bread and slave ale.

Word of your feast has spread, and entertainers are at your gates. A band of pit fighters offers a bloody show against beasts and slaves. A dark singer of Khaine offers songs of murder and war. A beastmaster offers his manticore, and swears he has it well in hand.
The pit fighters. Let blood flow.
The dark singer. Khaine deserves a hymn.
The beastmaster and his manticore.
No, I will not waste gold on such things.
Your guests arrive with their heavily armed retinues and kneel before your throne to renew their oaths. Each of them is counting your guards, your slaves and your enemies. The Feast of Khaine begins.
Welcome, all. Eat, drink, and watch your backs.
The table is spectacular. Slow-roasted hearts, wine from the plundered orchards of Tilea, and every delicacy torn from the far corners of the world. Your liege has spared no expense.
The food is good and there is plenty of it, with more than enough wine. It is not the finest table you have seen, but there is little to complain about.
The food is, to put it mildly, unimpressive. Fish, black bread, slave ale and cheap wine. Perhaps it is wiser not to say anything.
A table worthy of Naggaroth, dread liege!
Actually, this wine is one degree too warm.
You have set a fine table, dread liege.
I eat better than this at home.
*lie* Thank you for this feast, dread liege.
I will not eat slave food!
[From.GetFullName] loudly praises the bounty of your table and the quality of your wine to everyone within earshot.
You overhear [From.GetFullName] complaining about your food to the guests around [From.GetHerHim]. The gall. The insolence.
At least someone appreciates it.
I will remember that face.
The pit fighters you hired put on a spectacular show. They cut down every slave and beast set against them, and the sand of the pit turns red for the glory of Khaine.
The pit fighters your liege hired put on a spectacular show. Never have you seen such skill in the pits. They cut through slaves and beasts alike like true masters of the blade.
The dark singer begins her hymn, and your hall fills with verses of the Bloody-Handed God and his endless slaughter. Even your cold heart stirs as she sings of murder and eternal glory.
The dark singer your liege hired begins her hymn, and the hall fills with verses of the Bloody-Handed God. The haunting beauty of her song stirs your dark soul.
The beastmaster you hired puts on an excellent show. Monstrous beasts of every kind tear at each other and at the slaves thrown to them, and several novel ways of killing are demonstrated.
The beastmaster your liege hired puts on an excellent show. Monstrous beasts tear at each other and at the slaves thrown to them, and the guests roar with delight.
Gold well spent.
Magnificent!
The feast is over, and it was a triumph. As the last guests leave you sit back on your throne and smile, pleased at how everything turned out.
The feast is over, and it did not turn out as you had hoped. As the guests leave you sit alone in the hall and wonder who will pay for it.
I should do this again next year.
Next time it will be better. Or someone will bleed.
The feast is over, and it was magnificent. On the road home you decide that you would gladly come again if invited.
The feast is over, but certain unfortunate events spoiled it for you. On the road home you brood over the slights you suffered.
What a feast!
I will not forget this.

Late in the night you fall into talk with another guest and find a sharp mind and a shared hatred of the same rivals. You talk until the torches burn low, plotting how each of you might help the other rise.
I have made an ally tonight.
You spend half the night talking with [From.GetFullName] and find that you have much in common, not least a long list of enemies. Together you could achieve a great deal.
The wine flows, and one of the other guests has been looking at you with open contempt all evening. A Druchii does not swallow such insults. Your hand drifts to your blade.
I challenge you, here and now!
A guest will be challenged to a duel.
Not tonight. Not in my liege's hall.
[From.GetFullName] stands up, draws [From.GetHerHis] blade and challenges you to a duel in front of the whole court. The hall falls silent. Every eye is on you.
I accept. Draw your blade!
I will not fight a drunkard.
Your blade bites deep and [From.GetFullName] staggers back, bleeding. But [From.GetSheHe] is still on [From.GetHerHis] feet and comes at you again.
Your blade takes [From.GetFullName] across the face and [From.GetSheHe] reels, maimed. Yet [From.GetSheHe] will not yield and comes at you with the fury of the dying.
Then finish it.
You have wounded your opponent and won the duel. The guests applaud, and you have learned something about the blade tonight.
You have maimed your opponent and won the duel. The guests roar their approval as your opponent is carried out of the hall.
Your opponent lies dead on the floor of the hall, and you stand over the body with a dripping blade. The guests roar. Khaine has had his first blood of the feast.
Who is next?
Two of your guests have drawn blades in your hall. Before blood can be spilled you have your guards separate them. Neither of them will forgive the other.
Not at my table.
[From.GetFullName] wounded another guest in a duel at your feast. The guests talk of nothing else.
[From.GetFullName] maimed another guest in a duel at your feast. The guests talk of nothing else.
[From.GetFullName] killed another guest in a duel at your feast. Blood for Khaine, to be sure, but a dead vassal is a gap in your court, and the family will want someone to blame.
So be it.
The spouse of another guest has caught your eye across the table and has not looked away all evening. Your own consort is busy with the wine.
I should behave myself.
Send a slave with a discreet invitation.
An invitation is sent.
A slave slips a note into your hand. [From.GetFullName] invites you to [From.GetHerHis] chambers tonight, while your spouse is drinking with the other guests.
Why not?
Certainly not.
Some weeks after the feast, [From.GetFullName] is with child, and anyone who can count knows it is not [From.GetHerHis] spouse's. The court is full of whispers.
Let them whisper.
Your neighbour at the table fills your cup again before it is half empty and insists that you drink to your liege, then to Khaine, then to the Witch King, then to Khaine again.
To Khaine!
No more for me.
[From.GetFullName] refused to drink a toast at your table. Does [From.GetSheHe] think your wine is poisoned? Or does [From.GetSheHe] think [From.GetSheHe] is too good to drink with you?
An insult I will not forget.
You have drunk far too much. You knock over a candelabra, insult the steward's mother and then spill wine over half the table and the steward with it.
More wine!
[From.GetFullName] has drunk [From.GetHerHimself] senseless at your table and made a fool of [From.GetHerHimself] in front of the entire court.
Disgusting.
You wake with your face in a bowl of cold soup. The guests around you are laughing, and the slaves are trying very hard not to.
What are you looking at?
On the road to the feast your retinue was ambushed by outlaws who haunt your liege's lands. You escaped with your life, but not with your baggage, and you arrive covered in mud.
My liege will hear about this.
[From.GetFullName] complains loudly to anyone who will listen that [From.GetSheHe] was robbed by outlaws on the road through your lands.
Perhaps [From.GetSheHe] should have brought more guards.
A beastmaster has come to entertain your guests. He cracks his whip and barks commands at a towering manticore, and the hall watches spellbound as the beast seems to bend to his whip and his will.
Fascinating.

There is silence in the hall as the beastmaster works on the manticore. Then a shriek, and the beastmaster looks confused. The manticore has broken free of his will and is rampaging towards your guests!
Guards!

The whole hall is in panic as the manticore roars, smashing tables and tearing slaves apart. At last it spreads its wings and bursts out through your roof, but not before it has scared one of your guests half to death.
We are not hiring that beastmaster again.
The manticore came straight at you. You can still smell its breath, see its teeth an arm's length from your face. It took the slave beside you instead.
I need a drink.

The whole hall is in panic as the manticore roars, smashing tables and tearing slaves apart, until it pounces on one of your guests and rips them open. Then it spreads its wings and bursts out through your roof, leaving its victim a red ruin on the floor.
Woe!

The whole hall is in panic as the manticore roars, smashing tables and tearing slaves apart. The guests flee in all directions, except one, who draws his sword, leaps onto the beast's back, climbs to its head and drives his blade through its skull.
A hero among us!
When the manticore broke loose at your liege's feast, you alone did not run. You leapt on its back and drove your sword through its skull. The guests will be telling the tale for a century.
It was nothing.
The Sorceress

A murmur runs through your guests as a sorceress of the Dark Convent enters to entertain them. With a flourish she has a slave climb into a basket, then hacks the basket to pieces with a sword. When she lifts away the shreds there is no slave, no blood, nothing at all.
Amazing!
Guards, seize that witch!

A murmur runs through your guests as a sorceress of the Dark Convent enters to entertain them. She sets three cups before you, puts a black pearl under one, and moves them with blinding speed while she tells you to watch closely. Then she asks you to choose.
Left.
Middle.
Right.
The sorceress gives you a knowing, superior smile as she lifts the cup. It is empty. You chose wrong.
Well played.
Sorcery! You are cheating!
I saw your hand, witch. The pearl is in your sleeve.

A murmur runs through your guests as a sorceress of the Dark Convent enters to entertain them. She lays a rope on the floor and whispers to it. The rope rises like a serpent towards the ceiling, a slave child climbs it and vanishes into the shadows of the rafters. A moment later the child climbs down again, and the rope falls limp.
Amazing!
Hah! I saw the shadow-weave holding it up.
The night of Khaine has come. The guests walk across the bloodstained floor and bow before the statues of the Lord of Murder, whose iron hands drip red. The priests wait for your word.
Let the usual rites begin.
Khaine deserves more tonight.
Khaela Mensha Khaine, the Bloody-Handed God, the Lord of Murder, must be honoured with a great and bloody sacrifice. What will you give him?
A prisoner from my dungeons.
My finest slaves.
Ten manticores. We will paint the walls with their blood.

[From.GetFullName] screams as [From.GetSheHe] is dragged before the great statue of Khaine. Witch Elves hold [From.GetHerHim] down while one of them drives a long knife through [From.GetHerHis] heart. Then [From.GetHerHis] throat is cut and the blood is slowly collected in a great cauldron beneath the statue of the Lord of Murder.
A joyous night!

The slaves scream as the guards herd them in and drag them before the great statue of Khaine. Witch Elves hold them down and cut their throats one by one, and their blood fills the great cauldron beneath the statue of the Lord of Murder.
A Celebration in Blood

A great manticore is led into the hall, chained down and stabbed with spears, roaring and thrashing for long minutes as it dies. The guests watch in glee. Nine more follow, a long and bloody concert of death, until the floor is a lake of gore. Then Witch Elves step forward, slipping in the blood, dip long brushes into it and paint the walls until every stone is covered in dark, wet red. The smell is overpowering.
Praise Khaine, Lord of Murder!

The priests lead several Cold Ones beneath the great statue of Khaine and open their throats. The blood is gathered in bowls made from the skulls of slaves and carried through the crowd. A chant rises, then a roar, as the sacrifice to the Lord of Murder is made.

The feast is at its loudest when a shriek tears through the smoke-hole in the roof. A flock of harpies from the crags has smelled the blood and the meat, and now they drop into the hall on leathery wings. They rake the guests with their talons, tear roasts from the spits, knock over the braziers and foul the high table. One of them snatches a goblet of wine from your hand and screeches at you from the rafters. The feast hall is in uproar.
Shut the roof! Drive them out!
Hand me my crossbow.
Net one. I want to hear how it sings on the rack.
They like me! Look, they like me!
Such grace! Such a voice! I shall take one as my consort!
Ha! Look at the shrieking hags! Look at the steward's face!
Get those things away from me!
Harpy Consort
This lord keeps a harpy in their chambers and calls it their consort. The court laughs behind their back, and the priests of Khaine are not amused.
Ghrond

By decree of the Witch King, every woman who shows the gift for sorcery must give herself up to be trained in Ghrond, where the Convent of Sorceresses teaches the Lore of Dark Magic. She may take no husband and bear no children, and lives only to serve the Witch King as one of his brides. Your gift has been noticed.
I will give up all I have and go.
No! I can still hide it...
You could not hide your gift from the eyes of Naggaroth forever. The Witch King's servants have uncovered your secret and are dragging you to Ghrond in disgrace, as was always your duty.
It was good while it lasted.
Sorceress
Your daughter [From.GetFirstName] has the gift for sorcery and has been sent to Ghrond to study with the Convent. It is a great honour for your house: she will become a bride of the Witch King.
A great honour indeed.
Another daughter of a noble house, [From.GetFirstName], has been found to have the gift and sent to Ghrond to be taught by the Convent.
Good.
The trials of Ghrond are harsh and unforgiving. Only the most gifted and cunning of the summoned master the dark powers and claim their place as Sorceresses. The rest are broken.
I must keep learning.
You have spent ten years in the dark tower, and your work has paid off. You have taken your rightful place as a bride of the Witch King, a Sorceress of the Convent.

For all your efforts, you have not passed the trials, and the hags who rule Ghrond have not found you worthy to stand among them. Bound against your will, your mind is scoured away, and you are sent to the Witch King's court as a mindless servant to satisfy his lusts.
So I have.
Gooohhh...?
Your daughter [From.GetFirstName] has proven worthy of the title of Sorceress. She has taken her place in the Convent, bringing more honour to your great house.
Good for her. And for me.
Your daughter [From.GetFirstName] has disgraced herself. She failed the final trials of the Convent and has been reduced to a mindless slave in the Witch King's harem.
Disgusting child.
